entities.summary: The American Society for Mass Spectrometry (ASMS) is a professional association based in the United States that supports the scientific field of mass spectrometry. As of 2018, the society had approximately 10,000 members primarily from the US, but also from around the world. The society holds a large annual meeting, typically in late May or early June as well as other topical conferences and workshops. The society publishes the Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry. American Society for Mass Spectrometry is a learned society in Santa Fe, established in 1969. historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The American Society for Mass Spectrometry has had a significant impact on the development of mass spectrometry as a scientific field, with its annual meeting and publications contributing to advancements in fields such as pharmaceuticals and environmental monitoring. With over 10,000 members, it is one of the largest professional associations in the US.
